The FOMC paused at 5.25–5.50% and continued QT, emphasizing data dependence and elevated inflation risks—hawkish on balance. The Beige Book around this period reported modest overall growth, mixed consumer spending, flat-to-soft manufacturing, subdued housing, and weakness in office-related CRE. It also noted easing labor tightness with slower wage growth and some deceleration in price increases, while banks cited tighter lending standards and softer loan demand—corroborating tighter credit but also cooling inflation pressures. Taken together, the Beige Book tempers the hawkish tone slightly by indicating moderating wage/price pressures even as credit headwinds persist. Net tone: still cautiously hawkish and risk-aware, but marginally less negative than a SLOOS-only read.
